items.question: What is an eSIM?
items.answer: An eSIM (embedded SIM) is a digital SIM that allows you to activate a cellular plan without having to use a physical SIM card. It's built into your device and can be programmed with different carrier profiles.

items.question: How do I know if my device supports eSIM?
items.answer: Most modern smartphones support eSIM, including iPhone XS and later, Samsung Galaxy S20 and later, and Google Pixel 3 and later. You can check your device settings or visit our compatibility page for a full list.

items.question: How do I install an eSIM?
items.answer: After purchasing a plan, you'll receive a QR code. Simply scan it with your device's camera, follow the on-screen instructions, and your eSIM will be installed in minutes.

items.question: Can I use my regular SIM and eSIM at the same time?
items.answer: Yes! Most eSIM-compatible devices support dual SIM functionality, allowing you to use your regular SIM for calls and texts while using the eSIM for data.

items.question: What happens when my data runs out?
items.answer: You can easily top up your data plan through the Saily app. You'll also receive notifications when your data is running low so you're never caught off guard.

items.question: Can I share my data with other devices?
items.answer: Yes, you can use your phone's hotspot feature to share your eSIM data connection with other devices like laptops and tablets.

items.question: Do I need to be connected to Wi-Fi to install an eSIM?
items.answer: Yes, you'll need a Wi-Fi or data connection to download and install your eSIM profile. We recommend installing it before you travel.

items.question: How long does it take to activate an eSIM?
items.answer: eSIM activation is almost instant. Once installed, your eSIM will be ready to use within minutes.

items.question: Can I use Saily in multiple countries?
items.answer: Yes! Saily offers plans for 150+ countries. You can purchase country-specific plans or regional plans that cover multiple destinations.

items.question: What if I have issues with my eSIM?
items.answer: Our customer support team is available 24/7 to help you with any issues. You can reach us through the app, email, or live chat.

items.question: Is Saily secure?
items.answer: Absolutely. Saily is built by Nord Security, the team behind NordVPN. Your data and privacy are protected with industry-leading security measures.

items.question: Can I get a refund?
items.answer: Yes, we offer refunds for unused data plans. Please check our refund policy for more details or contact our support team.

whatIsMobileData.title: What is mobile data usage?
whatIsMobileData.description: Mobile data usage is how much internet you're burning through when you're not connected to Wi-Fi. It's the cellular data your phone pulls from network towers instead of your home router. Every scroll through Instagram, GPS search for the nearest cafe, or video call home eats into your mobile data allowance. For travelers, it's pretty important since you're often relying on cellular data networks instead of Wi-Fi connections.
whatIsMobileData.imageAlt: A happy woman activating her eSIM card on her phone.

items.question: What is data throttling and how does it affect my experience?
items.answer: Data throttling happens when your internet speed is intentionally slowed by your carrier or ISP. It often kicks in after you've used up your high-speed data allowance. The result is slower web browsing, longer photo load times, and choppy video calls. You can avoid the slowdown by picking a plan with more high-speed data.

items.question: How much mobile data do I need?
items.answer: How much mobile data you need depends on your usage habits — light users who only check emails and maps might need 1-2 GB for a week, while heavy streamers and photo uploaders may need 10 GB or more. Use our data usage calculator to get a personalized estimate.

items.question: How many GB of mobile data does the average person use per month?
items.answer: The average person uses 5-15 GB of mobile data monthly, but it varies widely. Streaming in HD uses three times more data than standard quality, and automatic photo backups can drain data without you noticing.

items.question: How many hours does it take to use 1 GB of data?
items.answer: Basic activities like web browsing and messaging use less data — you can perform these for dozens of hours per GB. For video streaming, 1 GB is usually enough for about 2-4 hours in standard definition. Music streaming is much kinder — you can get around 20-25 hours from 1 GB.

items.question: What activities consume the most data?
items.answer: Video streaming is the biggest offender — HD video can burn through 3 GB per hour. Music streaming uses around 150 MB per hour. Social media scrolling eats up roughly 100-200 MB per hour. Automatic app updates and cloud photo backups can demolish gigabytes in minutes.

items.question: Does browsing the internet use more data than using social media apps?
items.answer: In most cases, browsing the web uses less data than scrolling through social media apps. Simple websites with mostly text are gentle on your data. Social media apps are packed with auto-play videos, high-resolution photos, and frequent updates.

items.question: Why do I use so much data?
items.answer: Streaming movies or YouTube in HD is a classic data-usage culprit. Background apps can quietly munch through your data. Big downloads like games, updates, or cloud backups also add up quickly.

items.question: How can I manage data usage when traveling internationally?
items.answer: Check your carrier's international roaming rates before you leave. Turn off data roaming and use Wi-Fi whenever possible. The easiest way is to use our data usage calculator to estimate your needs, then get an eSIM data plan.

items.question: How can I use mobile data efficiently when working from home?
items.answer: Limit high-data activities like streaming during work hours. Only set up a mobile hotspot when necessary. Choose productivity apps optimized for low data usage. Turn off automatic app updates and cloud backups while on mobile data.

items.question: What are some good tips to reduce cellular data usage?
items.answer: Connect to Wi-Fi when available. Download content for offline use. Lower streaming quality. Enable data saver modes. Turn off automatic updates. Schedule app updates for Wi-Fi-only times.

items.question: What happens if I run out of data?
items.answer: Some plans cut off your data entirely until you purchase more. Others charge overage fees. With most eSIM services like Saily, you'll typically just lose access rather than face surprise charges. You can choose an auto top-up option or get a Saily Ultra plan for unlimited data.

items.question: How can I monitor my data usage on multiple devices?
items.answer: When sharing data across multiple devices through a hotspot, use your eSIM provider's app to track total usage. Configure data-saving settings on each connected device.

items.question: Can I share my data with other devices?
items.answer: Yes, you can share your eSIM data with other devices using your phone's mobile hotspot feature. Keep in mind that sharing data through hotspot uses your plan's allowance faster.

items.question: Do I use my mobile data when I'm connected to Wi-Fi?
items.answer: Usually, your phone sticks to Wi-Fi when connected. But watch out for features like Wi-Fi assist (on iPhones) or adaptive connectivity (on Android) that can automatically switch to mobile data if your Wi-Fi signal gets shaky.

items.question: Does my smartphone use data when I'm not using it?
items.answer: Yes, many apps run quietly in the background, syncing emails, refreshing feeds, sending notifications, or backing up photos. You can limit background data in your settings.

items.question: Does a smartphone use less data than a laptop?
items.answer: For most activities, smartphones use less data than laptops because mobile apps often compress images and videos. Laptops tend to load full versions of sites and larger files.

items.question: Which apps use the most mobile data?
items.answer: YouTube, Netflix, and Disney+ tend to use the most data, especially streaming in full HD. Social media apps like Instagram, Snapchat, and TikTok also rack up plenty of data with auto-play videos.

items.question: How much data does it take to download an app?
items.answer: A simple app might only be a few megabytes. More complex apps can exceed 100-200 MB. Large 3D games can reach several gigabytes.

items.question: Does updating an app use less data than downloading it?
items.answer: App updates usually use less data than a full download. Small bug fixes might need 5-50 MB, while feature updates can hit 50-200 MB. Major game updates can use hundreds of MB to gigabytes.

items.question: Do email apps use a lot of data?
items.answer: Email apps don't use much data for plain text messages (around 0.07 KB per email). Emails with large attachments can use up to 5 MB per email. Frequent syncing also increases data usage.

items.question: How much data does messaging use?
items.answer: Simple text messages use very little data (0.001-0.005 MB per message). Sending photos uses 0.1-2 MB per photo. Videos consume 500KB to 10MB or more depending on length and quality.

items.question: How much data do eSIMs use?
items.answer: eSIMs don't use any data themselves — they're digital SIM cards. Data consumption works exactly the same as traditional SIMs, depending entirely on your activities.

items.question: Does using an eSIM consume more data than roaming?
items.answer: No, data usage depends on your activities and network conditions, not whether your SIM is physical or digital. The advantage of eSIM is easier carrier switching and more affordable data rates.

items.question: How can I check my current eSIM data usage?
items.answer: On iPhone: Settings > Cellular. On Android: Settings > Network and internet > SIMs. In the Saily app, your current data usage displays prominently on the main screen.

items.question: How can I check my eSIM hotspot data usage?
items.answer: On iPhone: Settings > Cellular > Personal hotspot. On Android: Settings > Connections > Data usage > Mobile hotspot. Regularly checking helps manage your overall data limits.

hero.title: eSIM: What is it, and how does it work?
hero.subtitle: An eSIM is a digital SIM that's built into most modern phones. It works like a physical SIM card, but without having to insert anything into your device. eSIMs offer tons of benefits, such as helping you avoid roaming fees and making it easy to switch between providers.
hero.imageAlt: A happy woman activating her eSIM card on her phone.

definition.title: What is an eSIM?
paragraphs: An eSIM is an embedded subscriber identity module — essentially, a built-in chip in your phone. It does everything a traditional SIM would do, but without having to slot a tiny card into your phone. Additionally, an eSIM allows you to use several carriers and phone numbers at once, which is super convenient.
eSIMs are available on smartphones, tablets, smartwatches, and even some cars! They're great for quickly switching between phone numbers and grabbing mobile data for travel.

howWorks.title: How does an eSIM work?
howWorks.imageAlt: A man reviewing his Saily US eSIM plan on his phone.
paragraphs: An eSIM uses preinstalled software on your device to work just like a physical SIM. Once you activate it, you can connect to a cell network, make calls, and use mobile data. Most modern phones will have built-in eSIMs, but check our list of eSIM-compatible phones to see if yours does.
To start using an eSIM, just buy an eSIM plan and complete a quick setup. No need to remove your current SIM card — it can stay where it is, whether you decide to keep using it or not.

items.question: What does an eSIM card do?
items.answer: An eSIM is a digital version of a physical SIM card. It connects you to a mobile network, allowing you to make calls, send texts, and use mobile data. Instead of having to insert it into your device, you just need to buy an eSIM plan from a provider and activate it.

items.question: How can I get an eSIM?
items.answer: You can get an eSIM from any reputable eSIM provider, typically by making an online purchase. For example, Saily offers eSIMs in over 200 destinations — just find the country you want to use your data in and pick a plan.

items.question: Is eSIM better than a SIM card?
items.answer: In short — yes. eSIMs are built into your phone, so you no longer need to open it up to insert a tiny card. These virtual cards are great for switching between providers and for international travel. Without a SIM card slot, phones can be made smaller or have improved features (like a larger battery).

items.question: Why would I want an eSIM?
items.answer: You may want to get an eSIM for many reasons, like going abroad or needing extra mobile data to use in your home country. For example, if you're heading to a country where you can't get free roaming, buying an eSIM data plan can be an easy solution that won't break the bank.

items.question: Why are eSIMs not popular?
items.answer: eSIM technology is still quite new — the first eSIM-compatible smartphone was only released in 2016. Not many people know about eSIMs yet, and those who do typically use them with wearable and IoT devices only. That said, their popularity is growing as more people find out about eSIM benefits.

items.question: Is an eSIM safer than a SIM?
items.answer: Yes, in some ways. A physical SIM card can be damaged, lost, or stolen — especially if you're swapping out cards on your travels. eSIMs are electronic and built into your device, so you can't damage or lose them.

items.question: Does an eSIM give you a phone number?
items.answer: Not always. Some eSIMs (like the ones you can buy through the Saily app) only offer mobile data without a phone number, because you can do so much with data alone these days. However, some other providers give you a phone number with an eSIM.

items.question: Does an eSIM work without an internet connection?
items.answer: Yes, an eSIM can work without an internet connection. For example, with some eSIMs, you may be able to make cellular (voice) calls or send texts (SMS). What you can do with your eSIM depends on your eSIM plan and the provider you choose.

items.question: Does an eSIM drain your phone battery?
items.answer: Battery drain is not an issue with eSIMs, at least not more than with physical SIM cards. If your device has been using more battery power lately, it's likely caused by other apps on your phone.

items.question: Can you convert an eSIM back to a physical SIM?
items.answer: Yes, you can convert an eSIM back to a physical SIM — for example, if you want to use it with an older phone model. However, it's best to pop into your network provider's store to speak to an advisor and pick up a new SIM card.
